clue.text: Suddenly attacked by a state of ecstasy

definitions.meaning: to round on someone without warning is to assail them abruptly
slang for being thrilled or aroused, excited to a high pitch

explanation.surface: Someone is ambushed while in a blissful trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: one means rounded on violently, the other means excited or aroused.

clue.text: Old Ted resolved to have a little walk

indicators.note: resolved, read as broken down and re-formed, shows the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly Ted decides he will take a short stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' looks like decided, but it signals rearranging OLDTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with short unsteady steps, or to stroll casually.

clue.text: Think about having a male heir

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
a son is a male child who inherits

explanation.surface: Someone ponders having a boy to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' looks like the definition but 'about' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to use logical thought, to work things out.

clue.text: The Twelve retreat for cream pastry

parts.note: the European Community, abbreviated EC, had twelve member states at the time
a lair is a den or hideaway

explanation.surface: The apostles withdraw for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Twelve' suggests the apostles; it is the twelve-nation European Community of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux bun filled with whipped filling and topped with chocolate icing.

clue.text: How Thatcher worked and where thatcher worked free

definitions.meaning: Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister, worked in the House of Commons
a thatcher makes straw roofs, so works on top of a home
at no charge, paid for by the establishment

explanation.surface: Politician and roofer worked their respective places without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister 1979-90, sat in the House of Commons; a thatcher roofs cottages with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal phrases for working in Parliament and on a roof, and an idiom for something given gratis.

clue.text: Hundred held in check should be calm

indicators.note: something held in another is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: plaid is a checked tartan pattern
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people kept under control ought to stay peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as restraint, but it is the cloth pattern PLAID; C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and calm are synonyms describing an untroubled temperament.

clue.text: One who offers to board or disembark before a woman of title

parts.note: to land is to come ashore from a vessel
Lady is the title of a peeress or knight's wife

explanation.surface: A peeress either gets on or off a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests getting on a ship, set up by 'disembark'; it means lodging with meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who lets rooms and provides meals to lodgers.

clue.text: A sudden chill set in at the hair-dresser's no doubt

definitions.meaning: a spell of very low temperatures

definitions.text: set in at the hair-dresser's no doubt
definitions.meaning: a permanent wave produced with chemicals rather than heat

explanation.surface: A cold snap arrives at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in' sounds like weather arriving; a set is also a styled hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological term for a cold spell, and a chemical perm done without heat.

clue.text: They make fun of French jockeys

parts.note: de is French for of
jockeys are horse riders

explanation.surface: Some people mock jockeys from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like part of 'make fun of', but 'of French' gives DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockers: people who ridicule others.

clue.text: Decide by chance what busy artists do

definitions.meaning: settle a matter by picking straws or tickets at random
artists who are busy sketch a great deal

explanation.surface: A choice is left to luck, as hard-working painters keep sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A random selection idiom, and a literal phrase for producing many sketches.

clue.text: Rental review gives a bit of a buck

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, so the letters of the word are reworked

explanation.surface: A reassessment of a lease brings in some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' tempts as a dollar, so 'a bit of a buck' seems to be money; it is the male deer, whose horn is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male deer, and the branched horn grows from its head.

clue.text: Made a lot of lead initially electrically charged

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of lead is taken

parts.note: an atom given an electric charge has been turned into ions

explanation.surface: Plenty of metal was given an electrical charge from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a lot of' looks like quantity, but it means fussed over a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone as a celebrity is to make much of them, fêting them.

clue.text: Faulted in argument and utterly floored

indicators.note: utterly is read as 'when uttered', signalling a word said out loud

parts.note: floored, meaning knocked down, sounds the same in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Someone's case was weak and they were completely knocked flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'as spoken'; in British speech the two words are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument with defects in its reasoning is described as having flaws.

clue.text: Hunting young bucks carrying rifle across the chest

parts.note: bloods are fashionable young men
the military drill position 'port arms' holds a weapon diagonally in front of the body

explanation.surface: Young men with guns held across them go out shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' suggests the deer being hunted; here it is dashing young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting animals for pleasure is the classic example of a field pastime of that kind.

clue.text: Greatly impressed by what all-rounder did when not batting

definitions.meaning: overwhelmed with admiration or astonishment

definitions.text: what all-rounder did when not batting
definitions.meaning: a cricket all-rounder both bats and bowls; when fielding he delivered a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A cricketer who can both bat and bowl astonished everyone while his side fielded.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls delivered by one bowler, and an all-rounder is a player good at batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being astounded, and the literal cricket action of delivering six balls.

clue.text: Old boys treated and hidden from sight

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
cured as in treated by salting or smoking, or healed

explanation.surface: Former pupils got medical care and vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealed or made dim so that it cannot be seen clearly.

clue.text: Cosmetics to curry favour with the opposite sex

definitions.text: curry favour with the opposite sex

parts.note: make-up is face paint and powder

explanation.surface: Someone uses face paint to woo admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to flirt with or court someone.

clue.text: Father turns up in a trice for money

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad suddenly appears in a moment, asking for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' seems to mean arrives; it reverses PA to AP, which goes into ATRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: obtainable only at a cost, by paying.

clue.text: A mole tourists find attractive

definitions.meaning: a small dark mark on the skin, once thought fetching on a face
a scenic place that draws sightseers

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal seems to delight sightseers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests the animal or a spy; here it is the dark mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A facial mark considered fetching, and a picturesque site that draws visitors.

clue.text: Sift through a puzzle

definitions.meaning: to pass through a coarse sieve
a conundrum or enigma

explanation.surface: Someone works through a brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve used as a verb, and a word for a conundrum.

clue.text: Way out commercials for electrical units

parts.note: far means distant, a long way off
ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: Eccentric adverts promote electrical goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out' reads as weird; here it means distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of capacitance named after Michael Faraday.

clue.text: Was disposed to be treated as an invalid

definitions.meaning: was inclined, had a tendency
nursed, looked after as a patient

explanation.surface: Someone was inclined to be nursed like a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning inclined, and of one meaning nursed.

clue.text: Toadies engender a feeling of revulsion

definitions.meaning: sycophants who fawn on superiors
the shudder of disgust someone unpleasant gives you

explanation.surface: Sycophants make others feel sickened.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for obsequious people, and the noun for a shudder of unease, as in giving someone the willies.

clue.text: Reckon one million should be invested in property

indicators.note: put into something, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: an estate is a landed property
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A financier thinks a million should be put into real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested in' plays on finance but means placed inside: IM goes into ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate roughly, to judge an approximate value.

clue.text: Seek new marriage or patch up a broken one

definitions.meaning: to pair again, i.e. find another partner
to mend something damaged

explanation.surface: A divorcee wonders whether to remarry or save the old union.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as RE-PAIR, to couple up again.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful split meaning couple up again, and the ordinary verb for mending.

clue.text: Stop! Don't loosen your grip

definitions.meaning: an old command to halt, especially to a horse or rider
keep a firm clasp

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to halt and keep clinging tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation meaning wait or halt, and a literal instruction to clutch firmly.

clue.text: They buzz, but not with energy

definitions.text: They buzz, but not with energy

parts.words: They buzz, but not with energy
parts.note: male bees hum loudly yet do no work in the hive, so the word also means idlers

explanation.surface: Something hums constantly though it lacks any vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz with energy' is an idiom for liveliness; these hum literally but are famously lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Male bees buzz but do no work, and the word also means lazy hangers-on.

clue.text: Made much of being under considerable strain

definitions.meaning: emphasised, highlighted
tense and anxious from pressure

explanation.surface: Someone was fussed over while feeling very tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning emphasised, and an adjective meaning anxious under pressure.
